profile.address: 33 Thomas Street, Tribeca, New York, NY
profile.reading: Per the Wikipedia article on 33 Thomas Street, this New York City building (also known as the AT&T Long Lines Building) sits on the east side of Church Street between Thomas and Worth Streets in Tribeca, Lower Manhattan. It is 550 feet tall with 29 floors and was built from 1969 to 1974 as a telephone exchange facility housing long-distance switching equipment, designed for self-sufficiency with independent gas and water supplies and protection from nuclear fallout. The article states it currently operates telephone switching equipment and secure data centers, and reports that journalists have documented it as housing an NSA surveillance hub, a claim this session did not independently verify. This is a Wikipedia article, not an AT&T publication; no square footage or power capacity in MW is stated. Also known as the AT&T Long Lines Building, this tower was completed in 1974 after construction began in 1969, built for AT&T's long-distance telephone switching operations during the era before the 1984 Bell System breakup, when AT&T operated as a single vertically integrated national telephone monopoly. Its windowless, fortress-like design reflects Cold War-era resilience engineering: independent gas and water supplies, filtered air systems, and construction intended to withstand nuclear fallout, a design philosophy shared with a small number of other AT&T Long Lines switching buildings built in major US cities during the same period. The building remains active today housing telephone switching equipment and secure data center space, per the Wikipedia article on the building, though this registry does not independently confirm the specific tenants or the extent of AT&T's continued operational role at the address today versus that of other carriers or government entities reported by journalists to have equipment there. No square footage or power capacity figure specific to this building's current data center use was located in sourcing reachable this session.
